rules: Compare the Thriver only with themselves: no averages, rankings, percentiles or other Thrivers' wheels.
Nothing is overwritten: a pivot keeps the original and the new version, both dated.
Private by default; sharing is the Thriver's choice.
One level is one 30-day challenge. Every level's last day shows the same reveal, against Day 1 and the previous level.
Zones: 1 to 4 comfort, 5 to 7 growth, 8 to 10 thrive.

field_types.life_wheel: one 1 to 10 slider per life area, each showing its 1, 5 and 10 anchors

days.role: the honest starting point (moved from Day 2)
days.title: the honest starting point
days.quote: You do what you want, and for everything else you make excuses.
content: Honesty gives you a true starting point. Ownership turns it into ground you can build on.
Where you stand today is the sum of your choices.
Knowing each choice can be made again, or differently, is the key.
Like a map that has a “you are here” marker, so every journey has a beginning.
Today you mark your starting point. Tomorrow you choose your direction.
days.affirmation: I own where I stand, and I own where I go.

panels.text: Saved to Growth in your Progress tab: your starting point, dated today.

fields.prompt: Rate each area of your life as it stands today. Honest beats flattering: this is the line every gain gets measured against.
Which one area will you own this month?
Where have you been making an excuse? Name it plainly.

days.action: Copy down your one area and write the excuse beside it, before you close the app today.

action_proof.text: Across 138 studies, people reached their goals more often when their progress was tracked and written down.

days.title: meet your next best self
days.quote: You are the Hero of your own story.
content: The best version of yourself already exists within. Your Next Best Self awaits.
The space to THRIVE, a clear purpose and the ability to show up give every hero a standard to meet.
Heroes are made by decision: to act, to lead, to rise.
Yesterday you marked your starting point. Today you choose your direction.
days.affirmation: I decide who I become, and I start today.

panels.title: your starting point, beside your direction
panels.text: This is the gap you close. Day 30 shows how far you came.

days.title: success is a skill
days.quote: As much as talent counts, effort counts twice.
content: Success is a skill. This month you start to learn it.
Talent gets the credit. Repetition does the work.
Every skill you admire in someone else was paid for in reps.
Long hours, revising, planning, choosing the vision. Trusting the process.
Today you do your first rep. This life is more than a read-through.
days.affirmation: Success is a skill, and I am practising it today.

fields.prompt: Your first step, in one line.
How long will it take?
When will you do it today?

days.action: Do your step today at the time you named, then tick it off here.

days.title: your why
days.quote: Every one of us has a WHY, a deep-seated purpose, cause or belief that is the source of our passion and inspiration.
content: Your why is what gets you up on the days you'd rather stay down.
Motivation rises and falls. A strong reason holds steady.
When the why is vague, the excuses get specific.
Find a reason bigger than your excuses, and it will carry you on the days nothing else will.
days.affirmation: My why is bigger than my excuses.

fields.prompt: What sits underneath your why?
Why does this month matter to you? Write it, then ask “and why does that matter?” twice more.
Who gains when you become your Next Best Self?

days.action: Write your why in one sentence and read it aloud tonight, to yourself or to someone who will hold you to it.

days.title: discipline is a muscle
days.quote: Discipline is a muscle.
content: A muscle grows when you stretch it beyond the comfort zone, then give it time to rest. Repeatedly.
Discipline is built the same way: the step done before the scroll, the early night before the early start, the promise kept when nobody is checking. These are gains.
Every time you bargain your way out, you train the part of you that bargains. The opposite is equally as true.
Today do the extra rep, because every rep compounds.
days.affirmation: Every rep makes me stronger.

fields.prompt: The slightly harder version of your step today.
Which excuses will try to talk you out of it?
What will you say back? One line.

days.action: Do the harder version before 6pm today, and record it here once it's done.

changed: The anchor was plain logic, which the challenge format rules out. Your confirmed line, “Discipline is a muscle.”, now leads.
The muscle line moves to open the content block. Every other word stays as approved.

days.title: the promise
days.quote: If all you ever do is do what you say you're going to do, you will get through the thing that's uncomfortable.
days.quote_note: Australian ultramarathon runner and 2026 Young Australian of the Year, who ran 3,952 km across Australia in 47 days. Born 1999.
content: A promise kept to yourself is the foundation of self-trust.
You keep your word to everyone else. The person you let down most easily is you.
Writing it turns intention into commitment. Sharing it gives your word a witness.
From today, your word to yourself carries the same weight as your word to anyone else.
days.affirmation: I commit 100% to becoming my Next Best Self.

fields.prompt: Complete this: For the rest of this month, I promise myself…
Who will you tell?
On the day you least feel like it, I will…

days.action: Share your promise with one person today, and ask them to check in with you on Day 14.

days.title: build your system
days.quote: Often it's the simplicity of our own daily habits that we overlook in our efforts to achieve greatness.
content: Anything complex is simplified by a system, broken into bite-sized pieces. That is how this challenge gets done.
Your system starts with one habit: small enough to keep on your hardest day, big enough to create daily momentum.
Open your tracker in the Progress tab: find the gaps, and close them.
Last week you made the promise. This week you build what sustains it.
days.affirmation: I keep it simple, and I keep it daily.

fields.prompt: Pick the habit that starts your system.
Your habit, in one line, small enough for your hardest day.

days.action: Under 8? Make it smaller. Then do it today and tick it off here before you sleep.

days.title: design your space
days.quote: Environment is the invisible hand that shapes human behavior.
days.quote_note: American writer on habits and author of Atomic Habits. Born 1986.
content: Your space makes more of your choices than you do.
The phone by the bed, the shoes by the door, the bowl on the bench: each is a decision already made.
Leave the room as it is, and it keeps choosing for you. Design it so your new habits become the easy choice.
On Day 1 you pictured the space to THRIVE. Today you start building it, one object at a time.
days.affirmation: I design my space, and my space carries me.

days.title: learn from every day
days.quote: Success leaves clues.
content: Ten days in, every day has left you something: the days you kept show you what works, and any that slipped show you exactly where to build.
A missed day becomes a lesson the moment you review it to find why you avoided it.
How you respond is yours to choose. Read your days, and the road gets clearer with every one.
days.affirmation: When I learn, I build. What I build, I keep.

fields.prompt: What helped on your best days?
What got in the way on the harder days?
Your lesson, in one line: next time I will…

days.action: Write your lesson where you'll see it, and use it on tomorrow's habit, whatever today held.

action_proof.text: In a study of new habits, missing one day made no real difference to how they formed.
action_proof.source: Lally et al., European Journal of Social Psychology, 2010

flags: “Success leaves clues” is a common saying with no verified original (most often credited to Jim Rohn, popularised by Tony Robbins), so it shouldn't carry your name as an anchor. Option: “Life by design.” leads, and the saying moves into the content.

days.title: momentum over motivation
days.quote: If I only ran on the days I felt motivated to run, I wouldn't run very much.
days.quote_note: Australian ultramarathon runner and 2026 Young Australian of the Year, who ran 3,952 km across Australia in 47 days. Born 1999.
content: Momentum over motivation: you build momentum, and momentum drives motivation.
Motivation arrives when it likes. Your system arrives every day: one habit, one cue, one tick.
Routine is built on the days you least feel like it, and rhythm grows from routine.
Keep the system running, and motivation catches up with you.
days.affirmation: I keep the system, and the system keeps me.

fields.prompt: How steady has your system been this week?
What will your habit follow each day?
Your cue, in one line: After I ___, I will ___.

days.action: Do your habit today straight after your cue, and tick it off the moment it's done.

days.title: decide it in advance
days.quote: It is in your moments of decision that your destiny is shaped.
days.quote_attribution: Tony Robbins, Awaken the Giant Within (1991)
content: The hardest moment to decide is the moment you're in it: tired, rushed, tempted.
So decide now, while you're clear. When the obstacle comes, your answer is already waiting.
An excuse needs a gap to grow in. A plan made in advance leaves it no room.
On Day 5 you named your excuses. Today you give each one its answer, before it speaks.
days.affirmation: I decide before the moment decides for me.

fields.prompt: Which moment is most likely to stop you?
Your plan, in one line: If ___, then I will ___.

days.action: Put your plan in place today, and read it aloud twice before bed tonight.

action_proof.text: Across 94 studies, people who made if-then plans reached their goals more often.
action_proof.source: Gollwitzer & Sheeran, Advances in Experimental Social Psychology, 2006

days.title: one notch up
days.quote: Life is like riding a bicycle. To keep your balance you must keep moving.
days.quote_attribution: Albert Einstein, letter to his son Eduard (1930)
content: Twelve days of showing up have built something that carries you now: momentum.
Balance comes from moving. Every tick keeps you steady, and every kept promise makes the next one believable.
Today you add one notch to what you already do.
Tomorrow you look back at the road. Today you give it something worth looking at.
days.affirmation: I do better, I do more, I'm better than yesterday.

days.quote: When we are no longer able to change a situation, we are challenged to change ourselves.
days.quote_attribution: Viktor Frankl, Man's Search for Meaning (1946)
content: Two weeks of showing up have built your footing. Today you step into deeper water.
Everything you want sits on the other side of one task you keep moving to tomorrow.
Avoidance feels like rest. It costs more than the task ever would.
The task stays the same size. You are the one who grows.
days.affirmation: I move toward the work I've been avoiding.

days.title: the story you tell
days.quote: Self-sabotage is not moral failure; it's a safety strategy.
content: Every time you step back from that task, a story steps in to explain it.
I'm too busy. I'm not ready. It won't make a difference anyway.
The story keeps you safe, and it keeps you exactly where you are.
Today you write it down, word for word, so you can see it clearly.
days.affirmation: I see my story clearly, and I choose what happens next.

content: Yesterday you wrote the story down. Today you set its opposite beside it.
Both stories fit the same facts. Only one of them moves you forward.
You already hold sixteen days of evidence for the second one: ticks, lessons, kept promises.
The story you repeat becomes the one you live.
days.affirmation: The opposite is equally as true, and I choose it.

days.quote_note: American researcher and author on courage and vulnerability. Born 1965.
content: Courage is a decision made while the doubt is still talking.
Change asks you to be seen trying before you are sure it will work.
Every area you want to move into the thrive zone asks for a step that feels exposed.
Today you take yours, one size bigger than comfortable.
days.affirmation: I take the step while the doubt is still talking.

days.title: kindness keeps you going
days.quote: Worthy of greatness, capable of greatness and deserving of greatness.
content: Eighteen days in, some steps landed and some slipped. Both belong to you.
How you speak to yourself after a slip decides whether you take the next step.
Kindness keeps the standard high and the voice warm.
You hold the standard because you are worth it.

Your why has carried you through twenty days.
Every how you found since then came from that why: the system, the space, the plan.
Today you put all of it on the one area you chose to own.
